narration: Imagine surviving an atomic bomb.
visual: Black screen. A lone stickman fades in at center. A bright flash on the horizon; he braces.

narration: Now imagine getting on a train,
visual: The same stickman steps onto a simple train. Doors slide shut.

narration: traveling to another city…
visual: Train chugs along a dotted line between two city dots on a map.

narration: and getting hit by a second one.
visual: A second blinding flash. Stickman's jaw drops, "?!" above his head.

narration: Three days later.
visual: Calendar page AUG 6 flips to AUG 9. Big text: "3 DAYS".

narration: This actually happened.
visual: "TRUE STORY" stamp slams onto the screen.

narration: His name was Tsutomu Yamaguchi.
visual: Stickman with a name tag. Title text: "TSUTOMU YAMAGUCHI".

narration: In 1945, Tsutomu was a 29-year-old engineer
visual: Text "1945". Stickman in a hard hat holding a clipboard, label "29 · ENGINEER".

narration: who designed oil tankers for Mitsubishi
visual: Stickman at a drafting table sketching a big oil tanker blueprint.

narration: in his hometown of Nagasaki.
visual: Map of Japan, pin drops on Nagasaki, small house icon.

narration: That summer, his company sent him on a three-month business trip to Hiroshima.
visual: Stickman with a suitcase walks a dotted line Nagasaki → Hiroshima. Tag: "3 MONTHS".

narration: On August 6th, it was his last day there.
visual: Calendar: "AUGUST 6, 1945". Stickman packing his suitcase.

narration: Tomorrow, he'd finally go home to his wife and baby son.
visual: Thought bubble: wife stickman holding a baby in front of their house.

narration: That morning, he was walking to the shipyard
visual: Sunny morning. Stickman walks and whistles toward shipyard cranes.

narration: when he heard a plane overhead.
visual: He stops and looks up. Tiny plane high in the sky, "VRRR".

narration: He looked up and saw something drifting down on a parachute.
visual: Close-up: an object under a parachute slowly drifting down.

narration: Then,
visual: Freeze frame. Silence. Stickman's eyes widen.

narration: a flash brighter than the sun.
visual: Full-screen white flash; the sun icon looks dim next to it.

narration: He was about three kilometers from the blast.
visual: Diagram: blast point ↔ stickman, distance label "3 km".

narration: The shockwave threw him to the ground.
visual: Shockwave ring sweeps across; stickman flies backward and lands.

narration: His eardrums burst.
visual: Close-up of head, red zigzag at the ear, ringing "EEEEE".

narration: The left side of his upper body was badly burned.
visual: Stickman with left side of upper body highlighted red, burn patches.

narration: When he looked up, a giant mushroom cloud was rising over the city.
visual: Wide shot: tiny stickman, giant mushroom cloud over the city skyline.

narration: He spent the night in an air-raid shelter.
visual: Dark shelter at night, stickman huddled, moon outside.

narration: The next morning, he made his way to the station,
visual: Sunrise. Bandaged stickman limps toward a station sign.

narration: found one of the few trains still running,
visual: Crowded train puffing smoke, stickman squeezes aboard.

narration: and rode it home to Nagasaki.
visual: Train pulls in under a "NAGASAKI" sign; map line back home.

narration: Wrapped in bandages, exhausted, he had survived the unthinkable.
visual: Bandaged stickman slumped on a bench, long sigh.

narration: Surely, the worst was over.
visual: Stickman smiles faintly. Ominous music sting; sky darkens slightly.

narration: On August 9th, he insisted on going back to work.
visual: Calendar "AUGUST 9". Bandaged stickman walks into an office.

narration: He was telling his supervisor what he'd seen.
visual: Two stickmen in the office; Tsutomu gestures wildly. Window behind them.

narration: One bomb destroying an entire city.
visual: Speech bubble: one bomb icon → whole city crumbling.

narration: His boss didn't believe him.
visual: Boss with crossed arms, "?" over his head, eye-roll.

narration: "That's impossible," he said.
visual: Boss waves his hands; speech bubble "IMPOSSIBLE".

narration: "One bomb can't do that."
visual: Boss laughs and points at Tsutomu.

narration: And at that exact moment,
visual: Slow motion: the window behind them starts glowing.

narration: the room filled with the same blinding white light.
visual: Room whites out completely.

narration: Once again, Tsutomu was about three kilometers from ground zero.
visual: Same distance diagram as before, now in Nagasaki: "3 km… AGAIN".

narration: Somehow, he survived again.
visual: Stickman crawls out of rubble, coughing.

narration: His bandages were torn off, and he fell sick with fever for over a week.
visual: Stickman in bed with a thermometer; calendar pages flip through 7 days.

narration: But his wife and son had also survived.
visual: Family reunion hug, heart pops above them.

narration: And Tsutomu went on to live a long life.
visual: Years flip by on a timeline; stickman gradually ages.

narration: He had more children, worked as a teacher and an engineer again.
visual: More kids appear; stickman at a chalkboard, then back in a hard hat.

narration: And in 2009, the Japanese government officially recognized him as a survivor of both bombings,
visual: Old stickman receives a certificate "2009"; two bomb icons with checkmarks.

narration: the only person ever formally given that status.
visual: Spotlight on him, badge "ONLY ONE".

narration: In his later years, he traveled and spoke out against nuclear weapons,
visual: Old stickman at a podium speaking to a crowd; anti-nuclear sign.

narration: so no one would ever experience what he did.
visual: Children stickmen playing peacefully in a park.

narration: Twice.
visual: Big "×2" with two flash icons.

narration: Tsutomu Yamaguchi died in 2010 at the age of 93.
visual: Single paper crane; text "2010 · AGE 93"; slow fade.

narration: Some people call him the unluckiest man in history.
visual: Split screen left: rain cloud over stickman, "UNLUCKIEST".

narration: Others call him the luckiest.
visual: Split screen right: sun and four-leaf clover, "LUCKIEST".

narration: What do you think?
visual: Narrator stickman shrugs toward the camera, "?".

narration: Tell me in the comments and subscribe for more stories that sound too crazy to be true.
visual: Comment icon pops, then a subscribe button gets clicked. End card.
